A mock interview on CogniPrep costs one credit. You record answers to five questions, a background job processes them, and feedback comes back by email. If the job cannot finish, the credit goes back. That last sentence is the whole subject of this post, because "the credit goes back" has to mean exactly once, and a job that retries makes that harder than it sounds. It is a Trigger.dev task with ordinary retry settings: export const processInterviewTask = task({ id: 'process-interview', retry: { maxAttempts: 3, minTimeoutInMs: 2000, maxTimeoutInMs: 30000, factor: 2, randomize: true, }, run: async (payload) => { /* ... */ },

entry.title: Four Stripe products nothing ever buys, and a script that refuses to run against a live key
A DMARC report is mail no human reads, and ours was being forwarded anyway
entry.summary:
CogniPrep takes inbound mail through a Resend webhook. Someone writes to a support address, Resend posts an event, and our route fetches the raw message, parses the MIME, and re-sends it to the inbox a human actually reads. It is the same inbox the public help form posts into, which is the whole reason the forwarder exists: one place to look. Then we published a DMARC record with an rua= address on the same domain, and the forwarder started doing something silly. An aggregate report is an XML file describing which IPs sent mail claiming to be your domain, gzipped, attached to a mail whose subject looks like this: DMARC Aggregate Report Domain: {cogniprep.app} Submitter: {Amazon SES}
No person reads one of those. You feed it to a parser, or you look at a dashboard that has already parsed i…

entry.title: GrassLock: An In-Browser Open-Weight AI that Forces You to Touch Grass" published: true
entry.summary: What I Built The concept is simple: instead of doom-scrolling, you open GrassLock on your phone or laptop. The app blocks access to reward states until you physically walk outside and point the camera at live grass, a houseplant, or a tree. Once a nature object is recognized, the lock clears and records that you completed your outdoor break. Demo & Code https://dheerajharode.github.io/The-Offline-Touch-Grass-Verifier/ https://github.com/DHEERAJHARODE/The-Offline-Touch-Grass-Verifier/settings/pages Complete Data Privacy: The camera feed never leaves the user's device. No image frames or GPS coordinates are sent to an external server. Everything is evaluated directly in the browser's JavaScript engine via open-source MobileNet.
